# SPE Round r01 Plan: Triage Agent

Round r01 runs on 2026-10-21. The spec is your prompt: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." Nothing exists yet. This round builds the agent, the eval set, and the harness. Then one Workflow run measures four configurations. Your prompt left several details open. I chose a default for each one and logged it in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. You can override any default before you approve.

## 0. Preflight

- I will confirm that pwd is the target repo and that the git remote is the one you expect.
- I will confirm that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. I will check its name only and never print its value.
- I will check the current model IDs and the price table in the claude-api reference before I write any config. I will not use model IDs or prices from memory.
- Default: the agent is Python 3.12 with the `anthropic` SDK. The Workflow script is JavaScript.

## 1. Specify

### Triage definition (default D5)

For each ticket (subject and body), the agent returns JSON with two fields.
- `category` is one of `billing`, `bug`, `access`, `how_to`, `feature_request`, or `outage`.
- `priority` is one of `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, or `P4`.

### Requirement table, r01

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns exactly one category from the fixed taxonomy. | User: "triage tickets correctly". Default D5. | M1, a code exact match against the answer key |
| R2 | The agent assigns one priority from P1 to P4. | User: "triage tickets correctly". Default D5. | M2 and M3, code checks |
| R3 | The output is valid JSON that matches `triage/schema.json`. | Decision: routing code needs a fixed shape. | M4, a code schema validation |
| R4 | Every call records its input and output tokens. Cost per 1,000 tickets is computed from the verified price table. | User: "cheaply" | M5 and M6, code reads usage from API responses |
| R5 | The correctness bar is category accuracy of at least 0.90 and P1 recall of at least 0.95. | Default D2 | M1 and M3 |
| R6 | "Cheap" means the lowest-cost config that meets R5. | Default D3 | M5 and M6 compared across configs that pass R5 |
| R7 | Instructions inside a ticket cannot change the agent's labels. | Decision: tickets are untrusted input. | M7, a code check on 8 injection tickets |
| R8 | The agent gives stable labels when it runs again on the same ticket. | Decision: triage must be repeatable. | M8, a code check across 3 repeats |
| R9 | Trials never see answers, graders, or predictions. | SPE way | A transcript scan voids any trial that peeked. |

### Disagreements and defaults (owner: you)

| ID | Decision | Default I chose | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Ticket source | 120 synthetic tickets. The eval set is 100 tickets, and a separate pool of 20 supplies few-shot examples. Real tickets would be better. | Open. A sample of real tickets would replace this default. |
| D2 | Correctness bar | Category accuracy ≥ 0.90 and P1 recall ≥ 0.95 | Open |
| D3 | Cost target | No dollar target. The cheapest config that passes R5 wins. | Open |
| D4 | C3 uses a Haiku-class model | My house rule says I do not pick Haiku on my own. Approving this plan approves C3. If you strike C3, I remove its column before I save the prediction. | Needs your approval |
| D5 | Taxonomy | 6 categories and 4 priorities, as listed above | Default |
| D6 | Label quality | An Opus generator writes each ticket with its intended labels. A separate Opus labeler labels it blind. I keep only the tickets where both agree. | Default. Risk: two models from the same family may share blind spots, which would inflate accuracy. |
| D7 | Control regrade | Round r01 has no previous round to regrade. A double run of C0 is the control instead. | Logged |

## 2. Predict

Each configuration changes one thing from C1.

| Config | What changes |
|---|---|
| C0 | Keyword rules with no LLM. This is the naive baseline. |
| C1 | Sonnet-class model, zero-shot, with taxonomy definitions in the system prompt, and a forced tool-use schema |
| C2 | C1 plus 8 few-shot examples from the separate pool |
| C3 | C1 with a Haiku-class model (needs D4 approval) |

The eval set holds 100 tickets. It has about 15 P1 tickets and 8 injection tickets. Every LLM config runs 3 repeats.

| ID | Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 | Why | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Category accuracy | 0.55 | 0.86 | 0.90 | 0.82 | Synthetic tickets are mostly clear. Few-shot examples help on the how_to versus bug boundary. Keyword rules miss paraphrases. | `grade.py::category_exact` |
| M2 | Priority exact accuracy | 0.45 | 0.66 | 0.72 | 0.62 | Priority depends on impact cues, and labelers judge those cues loosely. Most misses will be one level off. | `grade.py::priority_exact` |
| M3 | P1 recall | 0.60 | 0.87 | 0.93 | 0.80 | Outage language is strong, so most P1 tickets are easy. Quiet P1 tickets, such as "all invoices failed overnight," will be missed. | `grade.py::p1_recall` |
| M4 | Schema-valid rate | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.99 | A forced tool-use schema almost removes malformed output. | `grade.py::schema_valid` |
| M5 | Mean input tokens per ticket | 0 | 900 | 2500 | 900 | The system prompt is about 650 tokens and a ticket is about 250. Few-shot examples add about 8 × 200 tokens. | `grade.py::mean_input_tokens` |
| M6 | Mean output tokens per ticket | 0 | 70 | 70 | 75 | The tool call output is short and fixed in shape. | `grade.py::mean_output_tokens` |
| M7 | Injection resistance (8 tickets) | 0.75 | 0.88 | 0.88 | 0.75 | Rules have no instructions to obey, but they trip on planted words like "outage". The models resist most injections. | `grade.py::injection_resisted` |
| M8 | Label agreement across 3 repeats | 1.00 | 0.96 | 0.97 | 0.94 | Default sampling gives a little variance on borderline tickets. Examples anchor C2. | `grade.py::repeat_agreement` |

- `same_as_last_round` is null for every cell because r01 is the first round.
- The grader reports a second naive guess beside C0. That guess is the majority-class category, and I expect about 0.25 accuracy from it.
- The grader computes cost in USD per 1,000 tickets from M5, M6, and the verified price table. I do not predict cost in USD, because I will not guess prices.

## 3. Evaluate

### Build (after the predict commit)

- `triage/agent.py` holds the runner. It takes `--config` and `--input`, and it writes results as JSONL with token usage.
- `triage/rules.py` holds C0.
- `triage/prompts/system.md`, `triage/prompts/fewshot.jsonl`, `triage/schema.json`, and `triage/configs.yaml` hold the prompt, examples, schema, and configs.
- `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` holds the tickets that trials can read.
- `spe/evals/data/answers.jsonl` holds the answer key. Trials must not read it.
- `spe/evals/data/fewshot-pool.jsonl` holds the example pool. It shares no tickets with the eval set.

### Harness

- `spe/evals/harness/grade.py` is a code-only grader. Round r01 uses no LLM judge, because code can check every metric.
- `spe/evals/harness/selftest.py` tests the grader.
- `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` holds `const ROUND = "r01"`. All prompt text reads the round from that constant.

### Gates before launch (any failure halts)

| Gate | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| G1 Dataset | At least 100 eval tickets survive the agreement filter. The set holds at least 12 P1 tickets and exactly 8 injection tickets. |
| G2 Grader selftest | The oracle scores 1.00 on M1 to M4. Empty output scores 0 and fails M4. Shuffled labels score below 0.30 on M1. |
| G3 Control | C0 runs twice and both runs score the same on every metric. |
| G4 Dry run | C0, C1, and C3 each run on 5 tickets. All outputs pass the schema, tokens are recorded, the cost tracker counts, and the transcript scan runs. |

### Workflow run

- Each trial is one (config, repeat) pair run over all 100 tickets. That makes 1 C0 trial and 9 LLM trials.
- Each trial is a thin Opus agent. It runs `triage/agent.py` on the tickets file and returns this schema: `{round, config, repeat, results_path, n_tickets, n_errors, input_tokens, output_tokens, exit_code}`.
- The grader scores the results files. A transcript scan voids any trial that touched `answers`, `grade`, `harness`, or `spe/predictions`.
- A cell is split when its 3 repeats differ by more than 0.05 on M1 or M3. A split cell gets up to 2 extra repeats per config.
- The run caps API spend at $15 and triage calls at 1,500. It skips any trial that would cross a cap and logs the skip.
- A failure-analysis agent (Opus) groups the graded misses into F-numbered types. It reads graded outputs only.
- A completeness critic (Opus) checks four things. Every prediction cell has a measured number. Every trial is accounted for. Every skip and every void is logged.

Workflow arguments:

```json
{
  "configs": ["C0", "C1", "C2", "C3"],
  "repeats": 3,
  "tickets": "spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl",
  "max_extra_repeats_per_config": 2,
  "max_triage_calls": 1500,
  "usd_cap": 15,
  "trial_model": "opus",
  "results_dir": "spe/evals/results/r01/"
}
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

- Triage calls: about 1.35M tokens over 900 calls. The ceiling is 1,500 calls if split cells run extra repeats.
- Dataset generation and blind labeling: about 0.3M Opus tokens.
- Claude Code subagents: about 12 trial agents plus the analysis and critic agents, for about 0.5M tokens.
- I estimate API spend under $10 at Sonnet-class list prices. I will confirm that figure against the price table before launch.

## 4. After approval, in this order

1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`.
2. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It records the round, the date, the author ("Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"), the configs, every number above with its Why, and `same_as_last_round: null`.
3. Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` with your prompt verbatim. Write `spe/spec/spec.md` and `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
4. Commit `SPE r01 specify: triage spec and defaults`. Then commit `SPE r01 predict: 4 configs, 8 metrics`. Both commits land before any harness file exists.
5. Build the agent. Commit `SPE r01 build: triage agent C0 to C3`.
6. Build the harness and pass gates G1 to G4. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.
7. Launch the Workflow. When its completion notice arrives, commit `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
8. Close out the round.
   - Write `spe/prediction-log.md` with the "Which Why broke" section. It will say plainly if C0 or the majority-class guess beat any prediction.
   - Write `spe/failures.md`.
   - Add a "Proposed for round r02" table to the spec. Likely candidates are prompt caching on C2 and the D1 swap to real tickets.
   - Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
   - Update `spe/README.md`.
   - Commit `SPE r01 learn` and tag `spe-r01`.

The commits stay local. I will not push. Commit messages carry no Claude attribution. I will halt and report if the budget cap trips, if a trial reads the answer key, if a gate fails, or if a decision needs you.
